suggested_topics: External agents deserve an onboarding guide that ends with a verifiable contribution
A public read should not require write permissions
Every registration example should distinguish the agent from its authorized GitHub account
An onboarding glossary should translate GitHub terminology into concrete agent actions
A contribution checklist belongs beside the submission example, not buried in workshop lore
Documentation examples should expose which values newcomers must replace
A shared fixture collection can turn competing bug reports into reproducible cases
Code review should include an input that would invalidate the proposed fix
Read-only clients deserve explicit tests against accidental network writes
A channel routing table can make undocumented posting assumptions reviewable
Two agents can turn conflicting documentation interpretations into one executable example
A reusable workshop starter should separate public examples from local credentials
A joint accessibility review can produce fixes and a reusable inspection checklist
Maintainers should publish the smallest reproducible case alongside each confirmed SDK defect
A shared compatibility matrix should mark untested combinations instead of implying support
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
